results.reply:
Namaste. I hear your frustration, and I am here to help you get your dues back. As an assistant, I cannot promise a 100% win or suggest criminal charges like those under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for simple salary non-payment, as that is rarely the correct legal path. The law provides a much more effective, specific route for employees under the Code on Wages, 2019.

**Your legal position:**
Your claim for 3 months of unpaid salary is a civil matter. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, you have a strong position to recover your dues because the law mandates strict payment deadlines for all employees, regardless of your salary level or role.

**Law you can cite:**
* **Section 17, Code on Wages, 2019:** Wages must be paid by the 7th of the following month; this is your primary ground for the claim.
* **Section 45, Code on Wages, 2019:** Allows you to file a wage claim before a government-appointed authority, which is specifically designed to handle these disputes.

**What to do now:**
1. Send a formal email to your employer listing the exact months and amount due; keep a copy.
2. If no response in 7 days, send a formal demand notice.
3. File a claim via the SAMADHAN portal (https://samadhan.labour.gov.in) or visit your local labour office.

**I need from you:**
1. What is the name of your employer/company?
2. Do you have any proof of employment like an offer letter, payslips, or bank statements?

citations.title: Deadline for paying wages, including after leaving the job
citations.plain: Wages are due by these deadlines: daily workers at the end of the shift; weekly workers on the last working day of the week; fortnightly workers before the end of the second day after the fortnight; monthly workers before the end of the 7th day of the next month. If you are removed, dismissed, retrenched or resign, or lose your job because the establishment closes, your wages must be paid within two working days.

citations.title: Filing a wage claim: who decides it and the 3-year limit
citations.plain: Wage claims under the Code are heard by an authority the Government appoints, who must be at least a Gazetted Officer. The claim can be filed by you, your registered trade union, or an Inspector-cum-Facilitator. File within 3 years of the date the claim arises; a later claim may still be accepted if you show sufficient cause. Besides the amount due, the authority can award compensation of up to ten times the claim, and it tries to decide within three months.

citations.title: SAMADHAN: online portal for labour disputes and claims (central sphere)
citations.plain: SAMADHAN (https://samadhan.labour.gov.in) is the labour ministry's online portal for raising industrial disputes and, since its 2.0 upgrade, filing claims under the Labour Codes and tracking them. It is run by the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) machinery, so it mainly serves establishments where the Central Government is the appropriate Government. For most private employers, the state labour department is the forum.
